subject: English
summaryPoints: Adverbs of manner describe how an action occurs; they are formed by adding '-ly' to adjectives (slowly, politely), with irregular forms sharing identical adjective/adverb shapes (early, late, fast, hard).
Adverbs of manner cannot be placed between a transitive verb and its direct object (e.g., 'He ate his lunch quickly', NOT 'He ate quickly his lunch').

Short agreement with positive statements is expressed using 'So + auxiliary/modal verb + subject', whereas agreement with negative statements is formed using 'Neither + auxiliary/modal verb + subject' (without additional negative particles).

Prepositions of time and place follow strict constraints: 'on' precedes specific days, dates, and surfaces ('on Monday', 'on September 11', 'on foot'); 'in' precedes months, years, seasons, and general enclosed spaces ('in 2023', 'in summer', 'in the morning'); and 'at' marks exact clock times, meals, and festival points ('at 8:30 a.m.', 'at night', 'at lunch time').
Word conversion morphology shifts word classes across nouns, verbs, and adjectives without necessarily altering root stems (e.g., advice -> advise, danger -> dangerous).

Punctuation marks fulfill distinct functions: parentheses (( )) enclose non-essential supplementary information or biographical dates; square brackets ([ ]) insert editorial interpolations into quotations; and braces ({ }) denote mathematical sets.

formulas.label: Positive Tag Agreement Formula
formulas.expr: Positive Statement  ->  So + Auxiliary/Modal/Do-verb + Subject Pronoun/Noun

formulas.label: Negative Tag Agreement Formula
formulas.expr: Negative Statement  ->  Neither + Positive Auxiliary/Modal/Do-verb + Subject Pronoun/Noun

formulas.label: Adverb of Manner Syntax Rule
formulas.expr: Subject + Verb + Direct Object + Adverb of Manner  OR  Subject + Adverb of Manner + Verb + Direct Object  (Never V + Adv + DO)

formulas.label: Prepositional Time Distribution
formulas.expr: at + precise time/points  |  on + days/dates/surfaces  |  in + months/years/seasons/centuries

examTip: Because 'neither' is inherently negative, never use a negative auxiliary verb after it in EUEE items. Incorrect: 'Neither didn't I' or 'Neither don't I'; Correct: 'Neither did I' or 'Neither do I'. Also note that 'fastly' and 'hardly' (as manner adverbs) do not exist; 'fast' and 'hard' are both adjectives and adverbs.

keyDefinitions.definition: A modifier that describes the condition, process, or style in which an action is performed, usually answering the question 'how?'.
A modifier indicating how often or repeatedly an event or routine takes place (e.g., always, frequently, seldom, never).
The morphological process of creating a new word belonging to a different grammatical class without affixational change.
Curved punctuation marks (( )) used to isolate explanatory, parenthetical, or qualifying remarks within a sentence.

eueeFocusTopics: Correct agreement structures using 'So do I' versus 'Neither do I'
Syntactic constraints on adverbs of manner (avoiding verb-object splitting)
Temporal and spatial prepositions ('at' vs 'on' vs 'in')
Morphological derivations between nouns, adjectives, and verbs
Phrasal verbs based on 'get' ('get along', 'get around to', 'get away', 'get back at')
